target_customer: Hospital pathology labs, oncologists and private insurers (Bupa, WPA, Healix) deciding on breast cancer chemotherapy
problem: Genomic recurrence tests for early breast cancer are costly and slow; Digistain scans routine tissue sections in infrared to give a prognostic score.
business_model: Per-test diagnostic fee through a UK laboratory and distributors
product_category: Breast cancer diagnostic test, medical device

founders.name: Hemmel Amrania
education: PhD, Imperial College London (doctoral researcher, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he scaled several seven-figure businesses in therapeutics and diagnostics

founders.name: Chris Phillips
founders.background_notes: Physics professor at Imperial per YC page

competitors.name: Oncotype DX (Exact Sciences)
competitors.what: Gene-expression recurrence test guiding chemotherapy, NICE-recommended

competitors.name: Prosigna and EndoPredict
competitors.what: Alternative genomic tests recommended by NICE in 2018

technical_complexity.rationale: Mid-infrared spectral imaging plus statistical modelling needed clinical validation and regulatory marking.

defensibility.rationale: Imperial-derived IP, a registered trademark (US registration 2024), UKCA marking and clinical data raise the barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents copying the method; Bupa, WPA and Healix adopted Digistain by 2024.

market_need_then: Genomic tests are expensive; the company claims a low-cost alternative with results in 1 to 2 days, supported by Imperial clinical data on 800+ patients.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clinical, hedged, not intended to replace clinical judgement

brand_strength.rationale: Brand appears as a product name in clinical press and a Product Hunt launch; no sourced mascot or community, and search gets confused with gaming firm Digitain.

outcome_analysis: Digistain turned Imperial College spectroscopy research into a UKCA-marked breast cancer prognostic test, raised about 1 million dollars in August 2022, and by late 2024 had insurer adoption and an Indian distribution partnership. Evidence of scale is limited to small seed funding and press, so it is an active medtech with regulatory progress but unproven revenue.
notes: Seedtable lists about $130K in Aug 2021 and CB Insights a $0.09M round in Apr 2024; both aggregator only, unverified. The $1M seed is confirmed by Nordic9 and Seedtable, which are aggregator-adjacent. Outcome search found no acquisition or layoffs. Name origin not found. Competitor sources are dated 2018 clinical literature, used for incumbents existing before the batch.
